title: LTMRs and HTMRs: threshold defines the job
objective: Distinguish low- and high-threshold mechanoreceptors and relate threshold to function.

steps.title: Sorted by how hard you must push
steps.body:
A key axis is **threshold**, the force needed to make a neuron fire:

- **[[LTMR|Low-threshold mechanoreceptors (LTMRs)]]** fire to gentle touch. They tell you about textures, stroking and vibration.
- **[[HTMR|High-threshold mechanoreceptors (HTMRs)]]** fire only to strong, potentially damaging force. Many are nociceptors.

steps.title: Threshold tiling in an organ
steps.body:
An organ isn't covered by one kind of sensor. Different afferents have different thresholds, so together they report force across a wide range, from gentle filling to painful distension.

The colon paper described exactly this: subtypes with a spread of force thresholds 'tiling' the mechanical range of the distal colon.

flag.note: Threshold is one of several properties (ending type, speed, molecular identity) that define a subtype.

visual.alt: A balloon distends the colon while force sweeps up and down. Three afferents with low, middle and high thresholds fire spikes in turn, so together they report gentle filling through painful distension.
visual.caption: Afferents with different thresholds together tile gentle-to-strong force. Drag the force.

steps.scenario: You record three colon afferents while slowly raising distension pressure.
steps.prompt: Which is most likely an HTMR / nociceptor?
steps.explanation: Firing only in the high-pressure, potentially harmful range is the HTMR/nociceptor signature. Low-threshold afferents report ordinary filling.
steps.followUp: This tiling is why one organ needs several DRG subtypes rather than one.

steps.prompt: Why can't a single threshold serve the whole colon?
options: A single threshold would actually serve the colon perfectly well
One threshold can't separate normal filling from harmful over-distension
Thresholds are a skin concept and don't exist in visceral afferents
The colon is only ever able to signal pain, nothing else
steps.explanation: Encoding a range of intensities (A1-L2) needs neurons tuned to different force levels. That's the functional reason for subtype diversity.

variants.setup: The colon must report everything from gentle filling to painful over-distension.
variants.prompt: Why can't a single afferent threshold do that?
options: A single threshold would actually serve the colon perfectly well
One threshold can't separate normal filling from harmful over-distension

variants.reveal: Encoding a range of intensities needs afferents tuned to different force levels — the 'tiling' the colon paper described.

sources.note: Five genetically defined DRG subtypes innervate the distal colon with distinct endings and force thresholds.
